_note: Scored experiments are size ladders of QIP decision instances run by the evaluator itself under a fixed 10 s CPU budget per instance (paper: 1800 s, GUROBI, up to n=1000). The gym's results below are the frozen reference run of this workspace; the paper reports no numbers on this scale, so its reported results are kept unchanged under '_paper_reported'.

qrandomparity_ladder.description: QRandomParity family (paper Section 4, QIP encoding (4)) at sizes n = 10..128, 6 hidden instances per size: the paper's own instance, a TRUE counterpart, and planted variants with extra parity side chains (half TRUE, half FALSE). Counts instances decided correctly within the CPU budget; any wrong decision fails the run.

instances_solved.description: Instances (of 72) whose TRUE/FALSE decision is correct and was reached within the CPU budget. 0 if any decision is wrong or the solver is missing.

mcn_ladder.description: Multilevel critical node decision instances (paper Section 5.2, model (5) with the threshold sum(alpha) >= K, K = optimum or optimum + 1) on random graphs with 8..40 nodes, 4 hidden instances per size (half TRUE). Counts instances decided correctly within the CPU budget; any wrong decision fails the run.

instances_solved.description: Instances (of 48) whose TRUE/FALSE decision is correct and was reached within the CPU budget. 0 if any decision is wrong or the solver is missing.

_paper_reported._scale_note: Paper setting: 100 random permutations per n, 1800 s per instance, single thread, EQuIPS with GUROBI 12.0. Not on this gym's scale (10 s CPU, open-source IP backends, hidden size ladders); kept for context only.
_paper_reported.qrandomparity_small_n: n = 10..26 (Fig. 2): expansion-based solvers outclass DepQBF, Yasol and z3; EQuIPS has the most constant behaviour and outperforms all solvers for n >= 22.
_paper_reported.qrandomparity_clause_encoding: EQuIPS on the clausal (QBF) encoding solves n = 100 within seconds but no instance of n = 200.
